claims.text: The investigated CoCrFeMnNi alloy is single-phase.
The coupled tribo-corrosion response is governed by competition between mechanical passive-film disruption and passive-film re-establishment.
Passive-film re-establishment is accelerated by diffusion along grain boundaries.
Ultra-fine-grained material has a higher grain-boundary density than coarse-grained material.
Higher grain-boundary density promotes faster repassivation.
Faster repassivation causes ultra-fine-grained CoCrFeMnNi to undergo less overall degradation than coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi.
Dynamic amorphization processing can produce both ultra-fine and coarse grain structures in single-phase CoCrFeMnNi.
Grain-boundary density influences passive-film formation, stability, and repair under mechanical disruption.
Sliding intermittently removes the passive film.
Grain boundaries provide accelerated diffusion pathways for selective oxidation in ultra-fine-grained samples.
Accelerated selective oxidation produces rapid repassivation of mechanically damaged surfaces.
The lower grain-boundary density of coarse-grained samples slows passive-film recovery and increases net degradation.
Ultra-fine-grained samples will have lower wear rates than the coarse-grained baseline.
Ultra-fine-grained samples will have lower corrosion current densities than the coarse-grained baseline.
Grain boundaries may act as preferential passive-film rupture sites and thereby negate the benefit of rapid repassivation.
The proposed behavior should hold at room temperature in acidic or chloride electrolytes when passive-film kinetics dominate.
The proposed behavior may fail at extreme temperatures or in environments that substantially alter oxidation and diffusion kinetics.
